questions.q: Why is a personal-data inventory required for erasure?

questions.explain: One procedure walks the inventory in dependency order: derived stores first (chunks, caches), then content (versions, messages, conversations, documents), anonymizing signal-preserving tables (feedback, training pairs) and retaining audit data per legal basis — with the request itself logged.
options: Walk the inventory in dependency order: derived stores, then content, anonymize signal tables, retain audit per legal basis — request logged
questions.q: How does the erasure procedure work?

questions.explain: Vectors are personal data (deletable via the tombstone path); backups age out on retention schedule or crypto-erase per tenant; training datasets are versioned so erased data never re-enters; replicas replicate erasure while app caches need explicit invalidation.
options: Embeddings are personal data, backups age out or crypto-erase, training datasets are versioned, caches invalidate by user
questions.q: What are the hard parts of AI erasure?

questions.explain: Per-category defaults (content: account lifetime + 30 days, derived: 90 days, prompt audit: 90 days, request audit: 7 years), legal-hold flags that suspend erasure for audit data, and scheduled retention sweeps sharing the erasure code path.
options: Per-category retention defaults, legal-hold overrides that suspend erasure, and scheduled sweeps on one code path
questions.q: How are erasure and retention reconciled?
